rules.check: Every consumed extension, including `omni.kit.commands`, is declared through the applicable direct runtime dependency or test dependency aggregator.
Every declared extension dependency has a remaining direct consumer import.
Every removed import has a targeted consumer-wide remaining-use scan with no stale reference.
Every removed module or package export binding has a targeted repository-consumer scan with no stale reference.
Every removed non-export public API member has a targeted repository-consumer scan with no stale reference.
Each third-party Python package added or retained by the change has one exact central pin.
Each third-party Python package added or retained by the change has documented compatible-license confirmation.
Each third-party Python package added or retained by the change remains integrated into the Flux pip archive build.
Every extension importing a third-party Python package directly depends on `omni.flux.pip_archive`.
A third-party Python package's Open Source Review Board (OSRB) record exists from addition through removal of its last repository consumer.
Third-party Python packages are supplied only by the Flux pip archive, never a standalone `requirements.txt` or direct installation.
Each changed intra-extension import is relative.
Each changed import alias is required by a real collision or an established external convention.
Each changed import binds every used symbol explicitly at module scope.

sources.section: Import the Symbol, Not the Path

rules.check: Each changed cross-extension symbol uses an absolute import from its nearest meaningful public package.
Every changed public Python namespace, including a test package's classes, is exactly defined by `__all__` and explicit package imports.
Every changed `omni.ext.IExt` implementation lives in `extension.py` rather than `__init__.py`.
